learningObjective: Distinguish correct claims about speculative decoding from common overclaims.

canonicalClaims.claim: Speculative decoding with proper rejection sampling preserves the target's sampling distribution exactly; its wall-clock win is largest when target-model decode is memory-bandwidth bound (batch-1) and shrinks when the target is compute-bound (large batch).
nonImplications: Does not require draft-target weight sharing.

misconceptions.claim: Speculative decoding gives a fixed (k+1)× speedup.
misconceptions.whyWrong: The bound is (k+1)×; actual varies with p and draft cost.

misconceptions.claim: Draft and target must share weights.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Only vocab/tokenization must match; drafts are typically much smaller unrelated models.

misconceptions.claim: Speculative decoding changes the output distribution.

implementationFacts: vLLM, TRT-LLM, SGLang all implement speculative decoding with configurable draft models.
EAGLE / Medusa use hidden-state prediction / additional heads as ultra-cheap drafts.
performanceScenarios: Batch-1 chatbot workloads see the largest wins; high-throughput batched serving sees smaller wins.
